# Purpose

This report documents Goal 5a of the RESI mixed-model extension project (see
`instructions/instructions.md` and `log/claudeLog.md` at the repository root):
a calibration check of the simulation machinery for `lme4::lmer` before any
RESI confidence-interval theory is layered on top. It collects, in one
place: the dataset used, the simulation settings, the diagnostics that
identified a fixed-effect SE mis-calibration under full bootstrap
resampling of the real data, and the **hybrid plasmode simulation**, which
is now the primary validation method for calibration going forward (see
the note below).

# Note: full bootstrap (plasmode) resampling does not produce consistent SEs

Earlier work in this project ran `longitudinalCalibrationSim()`, which
resamples the real `egsingle` data with a two-stage **with-replacement**
cluster bootstrap (draw schools with replacement, then draw children with
replacement within each drawn school) and refits Model A/B on each
resampled dataset. That full-bootstrap approach produced fixed-effect
model-based standard errors that were **not** consistent with the true
(Monte Carlo) sampling variability of the estimates: `mean_model_se / mc_sd`
plateaued well below 1 for child- and occasion-level covariates (`female`,
`black`, `hispanic`, `year`), and the between-school variance component
(`var_schoolid`) showed substantial, growing bias as the number of
resampled schools grew. This pattern held on both the real data and a
synthetic dataset generated from the same fitted model, and was not fully
resolved by decoupling the number of sites from the number of subjects per
site (see the diagnostic sections below for that history).

**Simon's hypothesis:** this failure is caused by real slope variation
across the sampling levels (e.g. schools and children have their own,
slightly different coefficients for covariates such as `year`, `female`,
`black`, `hispanic`) that is **not included in the model formula** (Model A
only has random intercepts, not random slopes, for these covariates). When
the real data is resampled with replacement, this unmodeled cross-level
slope heterogeneity is present in every replicate and inflates the true
sampling variability of the fixed-effect estimates beyond what the fitted
model's SE formula -- which assumes the random-intercept-only structure is
correct -- can capture. This is consistent with the slope-heterogeneity
diagnostic below, which found that removing true slope heterogeneity from
the data-generating process (a synthetic outcome simulated directly from
Model A's own fitted parameters, with no unmodeled heterogeneity by
construction) recovers correct SE calibration.

**The hybrid plasmode simulation (see the dedicated section below) is the
primary method used to validate calibration.** It resamples schools and
students hierarchically, preserving the empirical covariate distribution,
then generates new outcomes from the fitted Model A using rescaled empirical
BLUP pools and fresh residuals. Thus covariates are resampled, but real
outcomes are not; the generated outcome follows the specified random-
intercept model. Replicate fits now use REML. The earlier full-bootstrap
results and code remain available in `tests/` and `RESI/R/simulations.R` for
reference.

# Dataset: `mlmRev::egsingle`

`egsingle` is a 3-level growth-curve dataset (measurement occasion nested in
child nested in school) used as the plasmode base because it is the only
dataset found (across `lme4`, `nlme`, `geepack`, `mlmRev`, `JM`, `joineR`,
`merTools`) with >=1000 independent subjects, a continuous repeated-measures
outcome, and a continuous time covariate suitable for a smooth term.

## Overall size

```{r dataset-size}
size_tab <- data.frame(
  Quantity = c("Schools", "Children", "Measurement occasions (rows)"),
  N        = c(length(unique(egsingle$schoolid)),
               length(unique(egsingle$childid)),
               nrow(egsingle))
)
kable(size_tab, caption = "Overall dataset size")
```

## Children per school

```{r children-per-school}
n_per_school <- table(egsingle$schoolid[!duplicated(egsingle$childid)])
cps <- as.numeric(n_per_school)
cps_tab <- data.frame(
  Min = min(cps), `1st Qu.` = quantile(cps, 0.25), Median = median(cps),
  Mean = round(mean(cps), 2), `3rd Qu.` = quantile(cps, 0.75),
  Max = max(cps), SD = round(sd(cps), 2), check.names = FALSE
)
rownames(cps_tab) <- NULL
kable(cps_tab, caption = "Distribution of children per school (60 schools)")
```

Every one of the 60 schools has at least 5 children, up to 89, with a mean of
28.7 and median of 24 children per school (SD 18.1) -- a right-skewed,
moderately variable cluster-size distribution, which is why the plasmode
resampling below draws each school's *own* number of children (not a fixed
number) when it is resampled.

## Variables

```{r variable-table}
var_tab <- data.frame(
  Variable   = c("schoolid", "childid", "year", "grade", "math", "retained",
                 "female", "black", "hispanic", "size", "lowinc", "mobility"),
  Level      = c("3 (school, n=60)", "2 (child, n=1721)",
                 "1 (occasion, n=7230 rows)", "1 (occasion)", "1 (occasion)",
                 "1 (occasion)", "2 (child)", "2 (child)", "2 (child)",
                 "3 (school)", "3 (school)", "3 (school)"),

                 "continuous", "binary factor", "binary factor",

    "child sex", "child race indicator", "child ethnicity indicator",
    "school enrollment size", "% low income at school",
    "% student mobility at school"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
)
kable(var_tab, caption = "egsingle variables and nesting structure")
```

# Simulation design

## Fixed-divisor covariate rescaling

`size` (school enrollment, range 113-1486, SD 312.6) is on a very different
scale from the other covariates and caused an `lme4` convergence warning when
used raw. Both `size` and `lowinc` are rescaled by a **fixed divisor** (not a
z-score), applied identically to every replicate, so coefficients stay
directly interpretable:

- `size_100 = size / 100` (school enrollment in hundreds of students)
- `lowinc_10 = lowinc / 10` (percent low-income in units of 10 percentage points)

Combined with `lmerControl(optimizer = "bobyqa", optCtrl = list(maxfun = 2e5))`,
both models below fit with 0 convergence warnings on the full data.

## Models A and B

Shared fixed effects:
`math ~ year + female + black + hispanic + size_100 + lowinc_10`

- **Model A** (random intercepts only):
  `+ (1 | schoolid/childid)`
- **Model B** (random slope for `year` at the child level):
  `+ (1 + year | childid) + (1 | schoolid)`

The full-sample Model A fit uses ML (`REML = FALSE`) and supplies the plug-in
generating parameters and full-sample reference. Each simulated Model A fit
uses REML (`REML = TRUE`). Thus the replicate estimator is REML while the
full-sample target/generating fit is ML; interpret finite-sample differences
with that distinction in mind.

## Full-outcome two-stage plasmode bootstrap (deprecated)

An earlier version of this simulation resampled the real data directly in
two stages (schools with replacement, then children with replacement within
each drawn school). As documented in the note above, this full-bootstrap
approach does not produce fixed-effect SEs consistent with the true
sampling variability, so it is no longer used for calibration; see
`RESI/R/simulations.R` (`.longSimResampleHierarchical()`) for the
implementation if needed for reference.

Random-effect (variance component) standard errors are **not** computed by
any of the simulations below; only fixed-effect model-based SEs are
compared against the Monte Carlo SD of each fixed effect across replicates.
Variance-component point estimates are still tracked for bias.

# Hybrid plasmode (hierarchical covariate and BLUP resampling)

## Motivation and method

This hybrid plasmode resamples the covariate design hierarchically from the
real data, then generates fresh random effects and residuals from the fitted
Model A generator. This retains the empirical joint covariate distribution
across schools and students without carrying over the real outcomes.

For each replicate, draw `n_schools` source schools with replacement from
the 60 observed schools. Within each selected source school, draw students
with replacement. If source school $i$ contains $m_i$ observed students,
draw approximately $n_{per\_site} m_i / \bar m$ students, where $\bar m$ is
the average observed school size. Thus expected sample size is proportional
to source-school size and the average number drawn per generated school is
approximately `n_per_site`; rounding makes the realized total vary slightly.
Each selected student contributes all of their observed measurement rows.
Every school and student draw receives a new ID, even when the same source
school or student is selected more than once. This sampling is with
replacement and occurs anew for every replicate.

Raw BLUPs are shrunk toward zero relative to the true random-effect
variance (a well-known property of best linear unbiased prediction), so
each BLUP pool is first centered to exactly mean zero and then rescaled so
its variance equals the corresponding fitted variance component before any
resampling:
$$b^*_i = (b_i - \bar b) \times \sqrt{\hat\sigma^2 / \widehat{\mathrm{Var}}(b - \bar b)}$$
For Model A fit to the real data: the 60 school BLUPs have raw variance
0.056 (fitted `var_schoolid` = 0.079, so rescale factor $\approx 1.19$); the
1721 child BLUPs have raw variance 0.562 (fitted
`var_childid:schoolid` = 0.652, rescale factor $\approx 1.08$). The full-data
Model A fit remains ML (`REML = FALSE`) and supplies the plug-in DGP fixed
effects and variance components. School and student BLUP pools are centered
and rescaled to their fitted variances; each generated school and student
receives an independent draw with replacement from its corresponding pool.
Fresh residuals are drawn from the fitted Normal residual distribution.
Each simulated dataset is refit using REML (`REML = TRUE`); the coefficient
and RESI standard errors are model-based, from `stats::vcov`.

The reported grid is `n_schools in {15,30,60,100}` crossed with
`n_per_site in {25,100,200}`. The 200-school and 50-student/site conditions
are excluded. The simulation sets `set.seed(2026)` once before iterating over
grid cells. `mclapply` uses L'Ecuyer-CMRG worker streams with
`mc.set.seed = TRUE` for covariate resampling, BLUP resampling, and residual
draws.

## Results

Blank entries in the wide tables indicate conditions that were not simulated.
The RESI table reports the mean and SD of the realized student count across
replicates (`n` and `n_sd`), since proportional cluster-size sampling does
not yield exactly `n_schools * n_per_site` students in every replicate.
For the third plot row, the intercept and school-level predictors use
`n_schools`; student-level and time-varying predictors use the planned
student count `n_schools * n_per_site`. The realized student count and its SD
are reported separately. This follows the between-school versus within-school scaling
principle of Lyu and Welsh, treating repeated observations per student as
bounded for this comparison. The full-sample ML SE, scaled by the square root
of its full-sample reference count, is fixed across designs. Each cell's
Monte Carlo SD of coefficient error is scaled by the square root of its
planned count (`n_schools` for school-level terms; `n_schools * n_per_site`
for student/time terms), then divided by that fixed full-sample scaled SE.
Dashed curves show these ratios; the solid horizontal reference is 1.

```{r hybrid-fixedn-se-table}
fe2 <- hybrid_fixedn_summary[grepl("^beta_", hybrid_fixedn_summary$param), ]
wide2 <- reshape(fe2[, c("param", "n_schools", "n_per_site", "se_ratio")],
                 idvar = c("param", "n_schools"), timevar = "n_per_site", direction = "wide")
wide2 <- wide2[order(wide2$param, wide2$n_schools), ]
kable(wide2, digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "mean_model_se / mc_sd by fixed effect, n_schools, and n_per_site (hybrid plasmode, Model A)")
```

```{r hybrid-fixedn-beta-table}
kable(fe2[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "param", "truth", "mc_mean",
             "bias", "mc_sd", "mean_model_se", "se_n_level", "n_scaling",
             "n_reference", "truth_se_scaled", "mc_error_sd_scaled",
             "scaled_mc_error_sd_ratio", "n_success")],
      digits = 4, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Fixed-effect Monte Carlo estimates, bias, and scaled standard-error diagnostics")
```

```{r hybrid-fixedn-vc-table}
vc3 <- hybrid_fixedn_summary[!grepl("^beta_", hybrid_fixedn_summary$param), ]
vc3$rel_bias_pct <- 100 * vc3$bias / vc3$truth
widevc3 <- reshape(vc3[, c("param", "n_schools", "n_per_site", "rel_bias_pct")],
                    idvar = c("param", "n_schools"), timevar = "n_per_site", direction = "wide")
widevc3 <- widevc3[order(widevc3$param, widevc3$n_schools), ]
kable(widevc3, digits = 2, row.names = FALSE,
      caption = "Variance-component relative bias (%) by n_schools and n_per_site (hybrid plasmode, Model A)")
```

```{r fig-hybrid-fixedn, fig.width=14, fig.height=10, fig.cap="Joint hybrid plasmode calibration across n_schools and n_per_site. The third row shows scaled Monte Carlo coefficient-error SD divided by the fixed scaled full-sample ML SE; dashed term-colored curves are compared with the solid reference at 1. Intercept and school-level terms use n_schools; student/time terms use n_schools times n_per_site. Other rows show fixed-effect SE ratios, variance-component relative bias, RESI coefficient bias, and RESI ANOVA-term bias. Columns are n_schools values; y-scales are shared within each row."}

# Generate calibration figure directly from data (reproducible)
fe_terms <- unique(hybrid_fixedn_summary$param[grepl("^beta_", hybrid_fixedn_summary$param)])
vc_terms <- unique(hybrid_fixedn_summary$param[!grepl("^beta_", hybrid_fixedn_summary$param)])
resi_coef_terms <- unique(hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$term[hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$table == "coefficients"])
resi_anova_terms <- unique(hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$term[hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$table == "anova"])

.sim_pal <- c(
  "#1F77B4", "#D62728", "#2CA02C", "#FF7F0E", "#9467BD",
  "#8C564B", "#E377C2", "#17BECF", "#BCBD22", "#7F7F7F"
)
fe_cols <- setNames(.sim_pal[seq_along(fe_terms)], fe_terms)
vc_cols <- setNames(.sim_pal[seq_along(vc_terms)], vc_terms)
resi_coef_cols <- setNames(.sim_pal[seq_along(resi_coef_terms)], resi_coef_terms)
resi_anova_cols <- setNames(.sim_pal[seq_along(resi_anova_terms)], resi_anova_terms)

n_per_site.vec <- sort(unique(hybrid_fixedn_summary$n_per_site))
n_schools.vec  <- sort(unique(hybrid_fixedn_summary$n_schools))

row_limits <- function(values, reference = 0) {
  values <- c(values, reference)
  limits <- range(values, na.rm = TRUE)
  padding <- max(diff(limits) * 0.08, 0.05)
  limits + c(-padding, padding)
}

# Compute limits for each row
fe_limits <- row_limits(hybrid_fixedn_summary$se_ratio, 1)
vc_summary <- hybrid_fixedn_summary[hybrid_fixedn_summary$param %in% vc_terms, ]
vc_bias <- 100 * vc_summary$bias / vc_summary$truth
vc_limits <- row_limits(vc_bias, 0)
se_ratio_values <- hybrid_fixedn_summary$scaled_mc_error_sd_ratio[
  hybrid_fixedn_summary$param %in% fe_terms]
se_limits <- row_limits(se_ratio_values, 1)
resi_coef_bias <- hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$bias_resi[hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$table == "coefficients"]
resi_anova_bias <- hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$bias_resi[hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$table == "anova"]
resi_coef_limits <- row_limits(resi_coef_bias, 0)
resi_anova_limits <- row_limits(resi_anova_bias, 0)

# Set up multi-panel layout
layout(
  matrix(seq_len(5L * (length(n_schools.vec) + 1L)), nrow = 5L, byrow = TRUE),
  widths  = c(rep(3.4, length(n_schools.vec)), 2.0),
  heights = rep(1, 5)
)

# Row 1: fixed-effect SE calibration
for (ns in n_schools.vec) {
  sub <- hybrid_fixedn_summary[hybrid_fixedn_summary$n_schools == ns & 
                               hybrid_fixedn_summary$param %in% fe_terms, ]
  par(mar = c(2.8, 3.2, 2.0, 0.4), mgp = c(1.9, 0.45, 0))
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(n_per_site.vec), ylim = fe_limits,
       xlab = "n_per_site", ylab = "mean_model_se / mc_sd",
       main = paste0("n_schools = ", ns), log = "x", xaxt = "n", bty = "l")
  axis(1, at = n_per_site.vec, labels = n_per_site.vec, mgp = c(1.7, 0.35, 0))
  abline(h = 1, lty = 2, col = "gray40")
  for (term in fe_terms) {
    td <- sub[sub$param == term, ]
    td <- td[order(td$n_per_site), ]
    lines(td$n_per_site, td$se_ratio, col = fe_cols[[term]], lwd = 2)
    points(td$n_per_site, td$se_ratio, col = fe_cols[[term]], pch = 16, cex = 0.8)
  }
}
par(mar = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.5, 0.3))
plot.new()
legend("center", legend = fe_terms, col = fe_cols[fe_terms],
       lwd = 2, pch = 16, bty = "n", cex = 0.85, title = "Fixed effect")

# Row 2: variance components relative bias
for (ns in n_schools.vec) {
  sub <- hybrid_fixedn_summary[hybrid_fixedn_summary$n_schools == ns & 
                               hybrid_fixedn_summary$param %in% vc_terms, ]
  par(mar = c(2.8, 3.2, 2.0, 0.4), mgp = c(1.9, 0.45, 0))
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(n_per_site.vec), ylim = vc_limits,
       xlab = "n_per_site", ylab = "Relative bias (%)",
       main = paste0("n_schools = ", ns), log = "x", xaxt = "n", bty = "l")
  axis(1, at = n_per_site.vec, labels = n_per_site.vec, mgp = c(1.7, 0.35, 0))
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray40")
  for (term in vc_terms) {
    td <- sub[sub$param == term, ]
    td$rel_bias_pct <- 100 * td$bias / td$truth
    td <- td[order(td$n_per_site), ]
    lines(td$n_per_site, td$rel_bias_pct, col = vc_cols[[term]], lwd = 2)
    points(td$n_per_site, td$rel_bias_pct, col = vc_cols[[term]], pch = 16, cex = 0.8)
  }
}
par(mar = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.5, 0.3))
plot.new()
legend("center", legend = vc_terms, col = vc_cols[vc_terms],
       lwd = 2, pch = 16, bty = "n", cex = 0.85, title = "Variance component")

# Row 3: scaled MC error SD ratio
for (ns in n_schools.vec) {
  sub <- hybrid_fixedn_summary[hybrid_fixedn_summary$n_schools == ns & 
                               hybrid_fixedn_summary$param %in% fe_terms, ]
  par(mar = c(2.8, 3.2, 2.0, 0.4), mgp = c(1.9, 0.45, 0))
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(n_per_site.vec), ylim = se_limits,
       xlab = "n_per_site", ylab = "scaled MC error SD / ML SE",
       main = paste0("n_schools = ", ns), log = "x", xaxt = "n", bty = "l")
  axis(1, at = n_per_site.vec, labels = n_per_site.vec, mgp = c(1.7, 0.35, 0))
  abline(h = 1, lty = 1, col = "black", lwd = 1.5)
  for (term in fe_terms) {
    td <- sub[sub$param == term, ]
    td <- td[order(td$n_per_site), ]
    lines(td$n_per_site, td$scaled_mc_error_sd_ratio, col = fe_cols[[term]], lwd = 2, lty = 2)
    points(td$n_per_site, td$scaled_mc_error_sd_ratio, col = fe_cols[[term]], pch = 16, cex = 0.8)
  }
}
par(mar = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.5, 0.3))
plot.new()
legend("center", legend = fe_terms, col = fe_cols[fe_terms],
       lwd = 2, pch = 16, bty = "n", cex = 0.85, title = "Fixed effect")

# Row 4: RESI coefficient bias
for (ns in n_schools.vec) {
  sub <- hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary[hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$n_schools == ns & 
                                    hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$table == "coefficients", ]
  par(mar = c(2.8, 3.2, 2.0, 0.4), mgp = c(1.9, 0.45, 0))
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(n_per_site.vec), ylim = resi_coef_limits,
       xlab = "n_per_site", ylab = "RESI bias",
       main = paste0("n_schools = ", ns), log = "x", xaxt = "n", bty = "l")
  axis(1, at = n_per_site.vec, labels = n_per_site.vec, mgp = c(1.7, 0.35, 0))
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray40")
  for (term in resi_coef_terms) {
    td <- sub[sub$term == term, ]
    td <- td[order(td$n_per_site), ]
    if (nrow(td) > 0) {
      lines(td$n_per_site, td$bias_resi, col = resi_coef_cols[[term]], lwd = 2)
      points(td$n_per_site, td$bias_resi, col = resi_coef_cols[[term]], pch = 16, cex = 0.8)
    }
  }
}
par(mar = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.5, 0.3))
plot.new()
legend("center", legend = resi_coef_terms, col = resi_coef_cols[resi_coef_terms],
       lwd = 2, pch = 16, bty = "n", cex = 0.75, title = "Coefficient")

# Row 5: RESI ANOVA bias
for (ns in n_schools.vec) {
  sub <- hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary[hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$n_schools == ns & 
                                    hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary$table == "anova", ]
  par(mar = c(2.8, 3.2, 2.0, 0.4), mgp = c(1.9, 0.45, 0))
  plot(NULL, xlim = range(n_per_site.vec), ylim = resi_anova_limits,
       xlab = "n_per_site", ylab = "RESI bias",
       main = paste0("n_schools = ", ns), log = "x", xaxt = "n", bty = "l")
  axis(1, at = n_per_site.vec, labels = n_per_site.vec, mgp = c(1.7, 0.35, 0))
  abline(h = 0, lty = 2, col = "gray40")
  for (term in resi_anova_terms) {
    td <- sub[sub$term == term, ]
    td <- td[order(td$n_per_site), ]
    if (nrow(td) > 0) {
      lines(td$n_per_site, td$bias_resi, col = resi_anova_cols[[term]], lwd = 2)
      points(td$n_per_site, td$bias_resi, col = resi_anova_cols[[term]], pch = 16, cex = 0.8)
    }

}
par(mar = c(0.5, 0.3, 0.5, 0.3))
plot.new()
legend("center", legend = resi_anova_terms, col = resi_anova_cols[resi_anova_terms],
       lwd = 2, pch = 16, bty = "n", cex = 0.75, title = "ANOVA term")
```

## RESI point-estimator calibration

For each coefficient and ANOVA term, the table compares the full-data RESI
reference with the mean, bias, and empirical SD of replicate RESI estimates.
The reference uses the full-sample ML fit; simulated datasets are refit by
REML. Both use the same model-based covariance function (`stats::vcov`) and
student-level normalizer (`level = 2`), with the fitted student count `n`
recorded for each design. `Variation level` describes where the fixed-effect
design term changes. These metrics calibrate the RESI point estimator only,
not its sampling variance or confidence intervals; that covariance theory
remains future work.

```{r hybrid-fixedn-resi-calibration}
kable(hybrid_fixedn_resi_summary[, c("n_schools", "n_per_site", "table", "term",
             "variation_level", "n_level", "n", "n_sd",
             "n_success", "truth_resi", "mc_mean_resi",
             "bias_resi", "mc_sd_resi")],
  digits = 3, row.names = FALSE,
  caption = "RESI point-estimator calibration by term, n_schools, and n_per_site (hybrid plasmode)")
```

## Interpretation

- **Fixed-effect SE calibration and variance-component bias** are shown
  across the joint `n_schools` by `n_per_site` grid, with common y-axis limits
  across columns within each row.
- The RESI rows show coefficient- and ANOVA-term point-estimator bias against
  the model-based full-data target. These are point-estimator diagnostics;
  covariance and confidence-interval calibration for RESI remains future
  work.

# Open questions / next steps

- Simon's slope-heterogeneity hypothesis (see the note above) explains why
  full bootstrap resampling of the real data fails to produce consistent
  SEs, but has not been separately, directly confirmed for every affected
  term (it fully explains `year`'s mis-calibration in the earlier
  slope-heterogeneity diagnostic, but not the full extent of the
  child-level-covariate or `var_schoolid` patterns). In the current hybrid
  simulation, the covariate design is resampled but outcomes are generated
  from Model A, so no random slopes are introduced into the outcome model.
- The reported RESI uses the student-level count as a common normalizer. The
  calibration tables report the mean and SD of the realized student count
  under proportional within-school sampling.
- For 100 schools, source-school covariate profiles are sampled repeatedly
  from the observed 60-school empirical distribution. Assessing sensitivity
  to this finite school-profile pool remains an interpretation caveat.
